title: An AI-assisted command game about Korea and Vietnam: what changed after “follow history” looked like the obvious answer
author: Little_Education_256
selftext:
Hello guys,

I’m sharing Brinkmanship, a free browser command game during cold war made with generative AI for code and text. 

Playable here: [https://mgeoff1.itch.io/brinkmanship](https://mgeoff1.itch.io/brinkmanship)



In the Vietnam campaign, the historical option could look like the obvious answer even when it wasn’t the strongest one. Alternatives advertised their risks, but their longer-term benefits weren’t clear. That was a presentation problem as well as a balance problem.



The changes were to give historical plans dice rolls when they were real gambles, explain delayed consequences before the choice, and make alternative plans affect later decisions. The same approach was then applied to the Korean campaigns and the Pusan tutorial. The browser release uses decisions and sector allocations rather than tactical map battles.



The game uses plain JavaScript, separate campaign scripts and a Python release tool that rebuilds the English translation and checks packaged files. The current release is in English and French. Its period photographs come from public-domain archives.
